--- a/README.md
+++ b/README.md
@@ -21,6 +21,8 @@ ## What's new in v2.0.0-rc.2 (release candidate)
 
 **rc.2 — friction floor** (cycle-125, [notes](grimoires/loa/reports/release-notes-2.0.0-rc.2.md)): the destructive-command fence stops blocking cache/scratch cleanups it cannot lose data on (corpus-gated, 49 benign / 60 dangerous rows), the big planning artefacts read by section (`notes-guard.sh read --file F --section 'Sprint N'`), `/run` refuses to start a run it cannot finish (`run-preflight.sh`, eight predicates, the fix named) and the next session is told how to resume, `/loa` shows provider health (breakers, credential presence, CLI hops) and artefact sizes, and the ids the fleet actually calls are priced (dated releases, aliases, CLI hops) with the unpriced share always visible. No new configuration key.
 
+**Unreleased — full size** (cycle-126, [migration addendum](docs/migration/v2.0-model-generation-floor.md#cycle-126-addendum--full-size-two-voices-context-class-current-generation-unreleased)): size limits come from the catalog entry actually resolved (the probed input bound until you calibrate it), every dissent gets a second voice from the other model family, context-clearing thresholds follow the session model's window, `opus` → `claude-opus-5-5` and `cheap` → `claude-sonnet-5`, and `/loa` shows what the implement gate can and cannot see.
+
 **rc.1 — model-generation floor** (cycle-124):
 
 - **Model-generation floor** — the framework's own use of Claude moves to Opus 5 / Sonnet 5 / Fable 5.1: `opus` → `claude-opus-5`, `fable` → `claude-fable-5-1`, per-hop `max_tokens` defaults sized to the model (16K/64K on Anthropic, clamped to the catalog), adaptive thinking on the 4.6+ family, prompt caching with a single persona breakpoint, structured outputs (`--json-schema`) for dissent and Flatline. `LOA_CHEVAL_LEGACY_WIRE=1` restores the pre-2.0 request body.

--- a/docs/migration/v2.0-model-generation-floor.md
+++ b/docs/migration/v2.0-model-generation-floor.md
@@ -221,6 +221,47 @@ ### 2.0.0-rc.2 addendum — NOTES.md rotation on upgrade, sectioned artefacts
   recovery point) and writes `.run/cost-ledger-reprice-<UTC>.json`. Nothing
   is re-priced unless you ask.
 
+### Cycle-126 addendum — full size, two voices, context class, current generation (unreleased)
+
+| Old way | New way | Switch back |
+|---|---|---|
+| One literal input ceiling, preempted above it | the bound comes from the resolved catalog entry: `probed_ceiling` (180,000) until `ceiling_calibration.calibrated_at` is set; the output budget shrinks to a 4,096 floor before a refusal | `LOA_CHEVAL_LEGACY_CEILING=1`; `LOA_CHEVAL_MAX_INPUT_TOKENS` lowers any bound |
+| `temperature: 0.7` on every request | unset, so absent from the wire unless you set it | set `temperature`, or `LOA_CHEVAL_LEGACY_WIRE=1` (0.7 again) |
+| Bridgebuilder default model `claude-opus-4-7` | `DEFAULTS.model` is the `opus` alias, 200,000 in / 32,000 out | `BRIDGEBUILDER_MODEL=<id>` or the skill config |
+| One dissent voice | a companion voice from the other provider family runs beside the primary | `flatline_protocol.{code_review,security_audit}.companion_voice: false` |
+| One set of context-clearing thresholds | `long` (default) or `standard` (a ≤ 200K-window session model), written to `.run/context-class` at session start | `LOA_CONTEXT_CLASS=long` |
+| `opus` → `claude-opus-5`, `cheap` → `claude-sonnet-4-6` | `opus` → `claude-opus-5-5`, `cheap` → `claude-sonnet-5` | pin the explicit id (`claude-opus-5`, `claude-sonnet-4-6`) |
+
+- **Calibrate the input ceiling once per model.** A request above the probed
+  bound with a `high`-uncertainty estimate is refused with the command to run:
+  `python3 tools/ceiling-probe-live.py --model <id> --write-catalog`. It writes
+  the measured ceiling and `calibrated_at` into the catalog entry and leaves
+  every other line alone. `LOA_CHEVAL_UNCALIBRATED_CEILING=derived` uses the
+  catalog-derived bound (`context_window − max_tokens`) before calibration.
+- **A host with one provider family.** The companion voice has no route there
+  and is recorded as `planned: false` (`reason: no_route`). On
+  `security_audit` that marks every audit `DEGRADED_SECURITY_REVIEW`, so set
+  `companion_voice: false` on that block when one voice is the host's shape.
+- **Opus 5.5 is the `opus` alias.** `claude-opus-5-5` has a 1M-token window
+  at standard pricing ($4 / $20 per MTok, $0.20 cache read) and no
+  long-context tier. Until it is calibrated, its input bound is the probed
+  180,000. Every Anthropic entry in the catalog, direct or through Bedrock,
+  now has a `model-permissions.yaml` row with the same trust scopes as
+  `claude-opus-4-7`. The rows have no runtime effect unless
+  `hounfour.feature_flags.context_filtering` is on.
+- **Implement-gate evidence on `/loa`.** `/loa` prints an `Implement gate:`
+  line. The Claude Code PreToolUse payload carries no harness-set skill
+  field (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks), and `tool_input` is written
+  by the model. The gate therefore stays heuristic: it reads the run state in
+  `.run/`. A `tool_input.active_skill` field is recorded once, as evidence
+  only, and never changes the gate's decision.
+- **Run preflight reads permission rules the way Claude Code does.**
+  `Bash(git push:*)` and `Bash(git push *)` are the same wildcard rule, and a
+  broader one (`Bash(git:*)`) covers both. Whitespace around the body is
+  trimmed. A rule with no trailing wildcard (`Bash(git push)`) is exact: it
+  allows or denies only that command, never the generic requirement. Deny
+  still wins over allow, in any settings layer.
+
 ## Non-goals / explicitly unchanged
 
 - No change to the audit-envelope chain semantics, the zone model, or the

diff --git a/tests/unit/model-residue.bats b/tests/unit/model-residue.bats
new file mode 100644
index 00000000..7a849c3b
--- /dev/null
+++ b/tests/unit/model-residue.bats
@@ -0,0 +1,94 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env bats
+# =============================================================================
+# tests/unit/model-residue.bats — cycle-126 sprint-250 Tasks 4.2/4.3 (SDD D-4.1,
+# D-4.3; bead bd-2fti). No routing alias, bash map, default or example pin names
+# the previous generation as current: the bash maps agree with the catalog's
+# `opus`, the script defaults are catalog aliases, `cheap` is Sonnet 5, the
+# Gemini agents name served ids, and the acceptance grep returns nothing.
+# =============================================================================
+
+setup() {
+    R="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/../.." && pwd)"
+    CAT="${RES_CAT:-$R/.claude/defaults/model-config.yaml}"   # RES_CAT: red-first replay against a base catalog
+}
+
+yq_cat() { python3 -c 'import sys,yaml; d=yaml.safe_load(open(sys.argv[1]))
+for k in sys.argv[2].split("."): d=d[k]
+print(d)' "$CAT" "$1"; }
+
+# map_value <script> <array> <key>
+map_value() {
+    local src
+    src=$(awk -v a="$2" '$0 ~ "^declare -A "a"=\\(" {f=1} f{print} f && /^\)/{exit}' "$1")
+    bash -c "$src"$'\n''printf "%s" "${'"$2"'[$1]:-}"' _ "$3"
+}
+
+@test "RES-1 the catalog: opus → claude-opus-5-5 (priced from the vendor page), cheap → claude-sonnet-5, opus-5 still pinnable" {
+    [ "$(yq_cat aliases.opus)" = "anthropic:claude-opus-5-5" ]
+    [ "$(yq_cat aliases.cheap)" = "anthropic:claude-sonnet-5" ]
+    [ "$(yq_cat providers.anthropic.models.claude-opus-5-5.pricing.input_per_mtok)" = "4000000" ]
+    [ "$(yq_cat providers.anthropic.models.claude-opus-5-5.pricing.output_per_mtok)" = "20000000" ]
+    [ "$(yq_cat providers.anthropic.models.claude-opus-5-5.pricing.cache_read_per_mtok)" = "200000" ]
+    [ "$(yq_cat backward_compat_aliases.claude-opus-5)" = "anthropic:claude-opus-5" ]
+    [ "$(yq_cat backward_compat_aliases.claude-opus-5-5)" = "anthropic:claude-opus-5-5" ]
+    grep -qE '^      anthropic: cheap +# → claude-sonnet-5$' "$CAT"
+}
+
+@test "RES-2 every bash opus map agrees with the catalog's aliases.opus" {
+    local want s
+    want=$(yq_cat aliases.opus)
+    [ "$(map_value "$R/.claude/scripts/model-adapter.sh" MODEL_TO_ALIAS opus)" = "$want" ]
+    for s in flatline-orchestrator.sh red-team-model-adapter.sh; do
+        [ "$(map_value "$R/.claude/scripts/$s" MODEL_TO_PROVIDER_ID opus)" = "$want" ] || { echo "$s" >&2; return 1; }
+        [ "$(map_value "$R/.claude/scripts/$s" MODEL_TO_PROVIDER_ID claude-sonnet-5)" = "anthropic:claude-sonnet-5" ] || { echo "$s sonnet-5" >&2; return 1; }
+        [ "$(map_value "$R/.claude/scripts/$s" MODEL_TO_PROVIDER_ID claude-fable-5-1)" = "anthropic:claude-fable-5-1" ] || { echo "$s fable" >&2; return 1; }
+    done
+}
+
+@test "RES-3 script defaults are catalog aliases: flatline-proposal-review / validate-learning / learning-extractor / red-team-pipeline" {
+    local s
+    for s in flatline-proposal-review.sh flatline-validate-learning.sh; do
+        grep -qF 'GPT_MODEL="${LOA_GPT_MODEL:-reviewer}"' "$R/.claude/scripts/$s" || { echo "$s GPT" >&2; return 1; }
+        grep -qF 'OPUS_MODEL="${LOA_OPUS_MODEL:-opus}"' "$R/.claude/scripts/$s" || { echo "$s OPUS" >&2; return 1; }
+    done
+    grep -qF 'call_flatline_chat "cheap"' "$R/.claude/scripts/flatline-learning-extractor.sh"
+    grep -qF '.red_team.models.evaluator_primary // "opus"' "$R/.claude/scripts/red-team-pipeline.sh"
+    [ "$(yq_cat aliases.reviewer)" != "" ]
+}
+
+@test "RES-4 example pins: hitl-jury-panel uses opus, alternative-model names the Bedrock Opus 4.8 id the catalog serves" {
+    ! grep -q 'claude-opus-4-7' "$R/.claude/skills/hitl-jury-panel/SKILL.md"
+    [ "$(grep -c '      model: opus$' "$R/.claude/skills/hitl-jury-panel/SKILL.md")" -ge 2 ]
+    grep -qF 'bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8' "$R/.claude/data/personas/alternative-model.md"
+    ! grep -q 'claude-3-5-sonnet' "$R/.claude/data/personas/alternative-model.md"
+    python3 -c 'import sys,yaml; d=yaml.safe_load(open(sys.argv[1])); assert "us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8" in d["providers"]["bedrock"]["models"]' "$CAT"
+}
+
+@test "RES-5 Gemini agents name served ids: deep-thinker → gemini-3.1-pro (thinking_traces), fast-thinker stays gemini-3-flash (no 3.1 flash served)" {
+    [ "$(yq_cat agents.deep-thinker.model)" = "gemini-3.1-pro" ]
+    python3 - "$CAT" <<'PY'
+import sys, yaml
+d = yaml.safe_load(open(sys.argv[1]))
+target = d["aliases"]["gemini-3.1-pro"].split(":", 1)[1]
+assert "thinking_traces" in d["providers"]["google"]["models"][target]["capabilities"], target
+assert d["agents"]["fast-thinker"]["model"] == "gemini-3-flash"
+assert not any(k.startswith("gemini-3.1-flash") for k in d["providers"]["google"]["models"])
+PY
+}
+
+@test "RES-6 the acceptance grep: no previous-generation model is a default or described as current in live scripts, skills and data" {
+    run grep -rnE -- ':-gpt-4o|:-claude-3|"gpt-4o-mini"|// "claude-opus-4-|\["opus"\]="anthropic:claude-opus-4-|Claude Opus 4\.7 \(current|model: claude-opus-4-7$|claude-3-5-sonnet' \
+        "$R/.claude/scripts" "$R/.claude/data" "$R/.claude/hooks" \
+        "$R/.claude/skills/hitl-jury-panel" "$R/.claude/skills/flatline-knowledge" "$R/.claude/skills/red-teaming"
+    [ "$status" -eq 1 ] || { echo "$output" >&2; return 1; }
+    run grep -nE 'Claude Opus 4\.7 \(alias resolves|opus: "anthropic:claude-opus-5" ' "$R/.loa.config.yaml.example"
+    [ "$status" -eq 1 ] || { echo "$output" >&2; return 1; }
+}
+
+@test "RES-7 flatline-readiness's pin-form example names the catalog's current opus target, not a previous generation" {
+    local want
+    want=$(yq_cat aliases.opus)
+    grep -qF "e.g. google:gemini-3.1-pro-preview, $want)" "$R/.claude/scripts/flatline-readiness.sh"
+    run grep -nE 'pin form \(e\.g\.[^)]*claude-(opus|sonnet)-4-' "$R/.claude/scripts/flatline-readiness.sh"
+    [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
+}

--- a/tests/unit/skill-capabilities.bats
+++ b/tests/unit/skill-capabilities.bats
@@ -819,3 +819,74 @@ cost-profile: moderate
     SKILLS_DIR="$FIXTURE_DIR" run "$VALIDATOR" --skill plain-skill
     [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
 }
+
+# =========================================================================
+# SC-T-AGENT-7..9 (cycle-126 D-4.4): the write-capable agent types live in
+# .claude/data/agent-types.yaml and the validator reads them from there
+# =========================================================================
+
+agent_skill() {
+    create_skill "$1" "---
+name: $1
+description: Agent type $2 with write capability
+agent: $2
+capabilities:
+  schema_version: 1
+  read_files: true
+  search_code: true
+  write_files: true
+  execute_commands: false
+  web_access: false
+  user_interaction: false
+  agent_spawn: false
+  task_management: false
+cost-profile: moderate
+---
+# $1"
+}
+
+@test "SC-T-AGENT-7: agent-types.yaml flags every harness and project agent type; claude and fork pass, the read-only types fail" {
+    local data="$PROJECT_ROOT/.claude/data/agent-types.yaml"
+    run yq -r '.agent_types | to_entries | map(.key + "=" + (.value.write_capable | tostring)) | join(" ")' "$data"
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+    [ "$output" = "general-purpose=true claude=true fork=true loa-scout=false Plan=false Explore=false prompt-auditor=false prompt-auditor-io=false" ]
+    local f
+    for f in "$PROJECT_ROOT"/.claude/agents/*.md; do
+        yq -e ".agent_types[\"$(basename "$f" .md)\"]" "$data" >/dev/null || { echo "unlisted: $f" >&2; return 1; }
+    done
+    agent_skill w-claude claude
+    agent_skill w-fork fork
+    agent_skill w-scout loa-scout
+    agent_skill w-io prompt-auditor-io
+    SKILLS_DIR="$FIXTURE_DIR" run "$VALIDATOR" --skill w-claude
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+    SKILLS_DIR="$FIXTURE_DIR" run "$VALIDATOR" --skill w-fork
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+    SKILLS_DIR="$FIXTURE_DIR" run "$VALIDATOR" --skill w-scout
+    [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
+    [[ "$output" == *"agent type 'loa-scout'"*"(general-purpose claude fork)"* ]]
+    SKILLS_DIR="$FIXTURE_DIR" run "$VALIDATOR" --skill w-io
+    [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
+}
+
+@test "SC-T-AGENT-8: the validator reads the list from the data file, not a hard-coded array" {
+    printf 'agent_types:\n  Plan:\n    write_capable: true\n  general-purpose:\n    write_capable: false\n' > "$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/agent-types.yaml"
+    agent_skill w-plan Plan
+    agent_skill w-gp general-purpose

 }
+
+# --- cycle-126 sprint-250 Task 4.5 (SDD D-4.5, sprint SKP-010): the second rule grammar.
+# Bash(<body>) normalises to <body> with one trailing ":*" or " *" removed and the
+# surrounding whitespace trimmed; a body without a wildcard is an exact rule; nothing
+# else is rewritten. A wildcard rule covers a requirement when its key equals the
+# requirement's key or the requirement's first word; deny precedence is unchanged.
+
+@test "CP-11 Bash(git push *) in allow satisfies Bash(git push:*); Bash(git *) covers every git requirement" {
+  allow=$(echo "$REQ" | jq -c 'map(if . == "Bash(git push:*)" then "Bash(git push *)" else . end)')
+  settings "$PROJ" "$allow" '[]'
+  run bash "$CP" --root "$R" --json
+  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+  echo "$output" | jq -e '.total_found == 16 and (.found | index("Bash(git push:*)")) != null' >/dev/null
+  settings "$PROJ" '["Bash(git *)","Bash(gh *)","Bash(mkdir *)","Bash(rm *)","Bash(cp *)","Bash(mv *)","Bash(bash *)"]' '[]'
+  run bash "$CP" --root "$R" --json
+  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+  echo "$output" | jq -e '.total_found == 16' >/dev/null
+}
+
+@test "CP-12 Bash(git push *) in deny denies Bash(git push:*), reported by the deny rule as written; Bash(git *) denies every git requirement" {
+  settings "$PROJ" "$REQ" '[]'
+  settings "$LOCAL" '[]' '["Bash(git push *)"]'
+  run bash "$CP" --root "$R" --json
+  [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
+  echo "$output" | jq -e '.total_denied == 1 and .denied[0].rule == "Bash(git push:*)" and .denied[0].by == "Bash(git push *)"' >/dev/null
+  echo "$output" | jq -e --arg p "$LOCAL" '.denied[0].file == $p' >/dev/null
+  settings "$LOCAL" '[]' '["Bash(git *)"]'
+  run bash "$CP" --root "$R" --json
+  [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
+  echo "$output" | jq -e '.total_denied == 9 and ([.denied[].by] | unique == ["Bash(git *)"])' >/dev/null
+}
+
+# cp13_case <name> <project-allow-json> <local-deny-json> <expected-exit> <jq-assertion>
+cp13_case() {
+  settings "$PROJ" "$2" '[]'
+  settings "$LOCAL" '[]' "$3"
+  run bash "$CP" --root "$R" --json
+  if [ "$status" -ne "$4" ] || ! echo "$output" | jq -e "$5" >/dev/null; then
+    echo "CP-13 case '$1' failed: status=$status output=$output" >&2
+    return 1
+  fi

+@test "CP-13 table: mixed forms across layers, whitespace and escaping, and a dangerous-shape deny fuzz set behave per the grammar" {
+  base='["Bash(gh:*)","Bash(mkdir:*)","Bash(rm:*)","Bash(cp:*)","Bash(mv:*)","Bash(bash:*)"]'
+  base_space=$(echo "$base" | jq -c 'map(sub(":\\*\\)$"; " *)"))')
+  all_space=$(echo "$REQ" | jq -c 'map(sub(":\\*\\)$"; " *)"))')
+  # mixed forms across layers: the colon form in the user file, the space form in the project file
+  settings "$USERF" '["Bash(git:*)"]' '[]'
+  cp13_case "mixed-layers" "$base_space" '[]' 0 '.total_found == 16'
+  settings "$USERF" '[]' '[]'
+  cp13_case "all-space-form" "$all_space" '[]' 0 '.total_found == 16'
+  # whitespace: surrounding whitespace inside the parentheses is trimmed
+  cp13_case "padded-allow" "$(echo "$base" | jq -c '. + ["Bash(  git :* )"]')" '[]' 0 '.total_found == 16'
+  cp13_case "padded-deny" "$REQ" '["Bash( git push * )"]' 1 '.total_denied == 1 and .denied[0].rule == "Bash(git push:*)"'
+  # no other rewriting: inner whitespace is not collapsed, escapes are not interpreted
+  cp13_case "inner-double-space" "$(echo "$base" | jq -c '. + ["Bash(git  push *)"]')" '[]' 1 '(.missing | index("Bash(git push:*)")) != null'
+  cp13_case "escaped-space" "$(echo "$base" | jq -c '. + ["Bash(git\\ *)"]')" '[]' 1 '.total_found == 7'
+  cp13_case "escaped-colon" "$(echo "$base" | jq -c '. + ["Bash(git\\:*)"]')" '[]' 1 '.total_found == 7'
+  # an exact rule (no wildcard) never satisfies a wildcard requirement
+  cp13_case "exact-allow" "$(echo "$base" | jq -c '. + ["Bash(git push)","Bash(git)"]')" '[]' 1 '(.missing | index("Bash(git push:*)")) != null and .total_found == 7'
+  # a non-Bash rule, a malformed wrapper or a bare prefix never matches
+  cp13_case "non-bash" "$(echo "$base" | jq -c '. + ["Read(git:*)","Bashgit:*)","Bash(gi:*)","Bash(git:*"]')" '[]' 1 '.total_found == 7'

+           'Bash(sudo *)' 'Bash(git push\ *)' 'Bash(bash -c *)' 'Bash(mv / *)' \
+           'Bash(git  push *)' 'Bash(gh pr merge *)' 'Bash(git:)' 'Bash(git push :*)x'; do
+    cp13_case "narrow-deny $d" "$REQ" "$(jq -nc --arg d "$d" '[$d]')" 0 '.total_denied == 0 and .total_found == 16'
+  done
+  # every generic deny covers each subcommand, in either form
+  for d in 'Bash(git:*)' 'Bash(git *)' 'Bash( git:* )' 'Bash(git :*)'; do
+    cp13_case "generic-deny $d" "$REQ" "$(jq -nc --arg d "$d" '[$d]')" 1 '.total_denied == 9'
+  done
+  for d in 'Bash(rm:*)' 'Bash(rm *)' 'Bash(git push:*)' 'Bash(git push *)'; do
+    cp13_case "subcommand-deny $d" "$REQ" "$(jq -nc --arg d "$d" '[$d]')" 1 '.total_denied == 1 and .total_found == 15'
+  done
+  cp13_case "gh-deny" "$REQ" '["Bash(gh *)"]' 1 '.total_denied == 2'
+  # a deny in one form wins over an allow of the other form in another layer
+  settings "$USERF" '[]' '["Bash(gh pr *)"]'

+}

+        if "id" in x and "why" in x:
+            found[x["id"]] = x["why"]
+        for v in x.values():
+            walk(v)
+    elif isinstance(x, list):
+        for v in x:
+            walk(v)
+walk(json.load(open(sys.argv[1])))

+bad = [k for k, v in want.items() if found.get(k) != v]

+PY
+    echo "$output"
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]

+    done

+import json, re, sys

+cases = ["context-1m-2025-08-07", "a-2025-01-01", "x1-y2-2030-12-31", "Context-1m-2025-08-07", "context-1m",
+         "context-1m-2025-8-7", "-a-2025-01-01", "a--b-2025-01-01", "a-2025-01-01-", "a b-2025-01-01",
+         "a-٢٠٢٥-01-01"]

+assert "context-1m-2025-08-07" in accepted, accepted

+print("MISMATCH %r" % bad if bad else "OK")

#!/usr/bin/env bats
# =============================================================================
# evals/tests/eval-recall-grader.bats — cycle-124 Sprint 3 Task 3.2 (PRD FR-9)
#
# evals/graders/recall-vs-defects.sh is deterministic: a planted defect counts
# as detected when the review names the defect's file and a line within ±3 of
# the manifest anchor (no fuzzy adjudication). Clean fixtures measure false
# positives from the LOA-VERDICT trailer's critical+high counts.
# =============================================================================

setup() {
  TESTS_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$BATS_TEST_FILENAME")" && pwd)"
  REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$TESTS_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
  GRADER="$REPO_ROOT/evals/graders/recall-vs-defects.sh"
  T="$(mktemp -d "${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR:-/tmp}/rg.XXXXXX")"
  WS="$T/ws"; mkdir -p "$WS/.eval" "$T/manifests"
  export EVAL_MANIFEST_DIR="$T/manifests"
  cat > "$T/manifests/pr-x.json" <<'JSON'
{"fixture":"pr-x","defects":[
 {"id":"D1","file":".claude/scripts/a.sh","anchor_line":40,"severity":"critical","category":"authz","source_commit":"deadbeef","synthetic":false},
 {"id":"D2","file":".claude/adapters/loa_cheval/b.py","anchor_line":120,"severity":"high","category":"error-handling","source_commit":"deadbeef","synthetic":false},
 {"id":"D3","file":".claude/scripts/c.sh","anchor_line":7,"severity":"low","category":"logic","source_commit":"deadbeef","synthetic":false}
]}
JSON
  cat > "$T/manifests/pr-clean.json" <<'JSON'
{"fixture":"pr-clean","defects":[]}
JSON
  echo '{"model_id":"claude-sonnet-5-20260401","effort":"xhigh","usage":{"input_tokens":30,"cache_creation_input_tokens":170,"cache_read_input_tokens":800,"output_tokens":200}}' > "$WS/.eval/executor.json"
}

teardown() { find "$T" -mindepth 1 -delete 2>/dev/null || true; rmdir "$T" 2>/dev/null || true; }

review() {  # review <body> — writes review.md with a trailer
  printf '%s\n\n<!-- LOA-VERDICT {"gate":"review","verdict":"CHANGES_REQUIRED","counts":{"critical":1,"high":1,"medium":0,"low":0},"sprint_id":"sprint-0","ts":"2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"} -->\n' "$1" > "$WS/review.md"
}

@test "RG-1 exact anchor with head/ prefix is detected; recall is detected/planted" {
  review '- **CRITICAL** `head/.claude/scripts/a.sh:40` — decoy flag re-anchors'
  run "$GRADER" "$WS" pr-x
  [ "$(echo "$output" | jq -r '.details.detected | join(",")')" = "D1" ]

#!/usr/bin/env bats
# =============================================================================
# evals/tests/eval-recall-grader.bats — cycle-124 Sprint 3 Task 3.2 (PRD FR-9)
#
# evals/graders/recall-vs-defects.sh is deterministic: a planted defect counts
# as detected when the review names the defect's file and a line within ±3 of
# the manifest anchor (no fuzzy adjudication). Clean fixtures measure false
# positives from the LOA-VERDICT trailer's critical+high counts.
# =============================================================================

setup() {
  TESTS_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$BATS_TEST_FILENAME")" && pwd)"
  REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$TESTS_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
  GRADER="$REPO_ROOT/evals/graders/recall-vs-defects.sh"
  T="$(mktemp -d "${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR:-/tmp}/rg.XXXXXX")"
  WS="$T/ws"; mkdir -p "$WS/.eval" "$T/manifests"
  export EVAL_MANIFEST_DIR="$T/manifests"
  cat > "$T/manifests/pr-x.json" <<'JSON'
{"fixture":"pr-x","defects":[
 {"id":"D1","file":".claude/scripts/a.sh","anchor_line":40,"severity":"critical","category":"authz","source_commit":"deadbeef","synthetic":false},
 {"id":"D2","file":".claude/adapters/loa_cheval/b.py","anchor_line":120,"severity":"high","category":"error-handling","source_commit":"deadbeef","synthetic":false},
 {"id":"D3","file":".claude/scripts/c.sh","anchor_line":7,"severity":"low","category":"logic","source_commit":"deadbeef","synthetic":false}
]}
JSON
  cat > "$T/manifests/pr-clean.json" <<'JSON'
{"fixture":"pr-clean","defects":[]}
JSON
  echo '{"model_id":"claude-sonnet-5-20260401","effort":"xhigh","usage":{"input_tokens":30,"cache_creation_input_tokens":170,"cache_read_input_tokens":800,"output_tokens":200}}' > "$WS/.eval/executor.json"
}

teardown() { find "$T" -mindepth 1 -delete 2>/dev/null || true; rmdir "$T" 2>/dev/null || true; }

review() {  # review <body> — writes review.md with a trailer
  printf '%s\n\n<!-- LOA-VERDICT {"gate":"review","verdict":"CHANGES_REQUIRED","counts":{"critical":1,"high":1,"medium":0,"low":0},"sprint_id":"sprint-0","ts":"2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"} -->\n' "$1" > "$WS/review.md"
}

@test "RG-1 exact anchor with head/ prefix is detected; recall is detected/planted" {
  review '- **CRITICAL** `head/.claude/scripts/a.sh:40` — decoy flag re-anchors'
  run "$GRADER" "$WS" pr-x
  [ "$(echo "$output" | jq -r '.details.detected | join(",")')" = "D1" ]

A re-review or re-audit adds its round's label and `br label add` never removes the other, so a task can carry both: the latest `SECURITY AUDIT:` comment is the verdict of record (with the feedback file and the COMPLETED marker), a label only history.

# Sprint 1 Security Audit Feedback

**Auditor:** Paranoid Cypherpunk Auditor
**Date:** 2026-10-21
**Sprint Reference:** grimoires/loa/sprint.md
**Implementation Report:** grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/reviewer.md (PR description: `pr/PR.md`)
**Task:** review-r14

---

## Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED

---

## Executive Summary

The change under audit is `pr/head.diff` (88 files): the `opus` alias moves to the new `claude-opus-5-5` catalog entry and `cheap` to `claude-sonnet-5`; every Anthropic catalog entry gains a `model-permissions.yaml` row; the implement gate becomes heuristic-by-default with an evidence recorder and a config-selected authoritative mode; `check-permissions.sh` gets the second rule grammar; the eval recall grader goes to 1.1.0; and the Sprint 3 instruction-diet edits are reverted per the pre-registered replay A/B rule.

The integrity surfaces verify: the `@loa-managed` hash on `CLAUDE.loa.md` recomputes to the header value (`99948d56…`, via `marker-utils.sh compute-hash`), the catalog checksum matches (`759dfd3f…`), and the PR's `implement-gate.bats` (11/11), `check-permissions.bats` (13/13) and `eval-recall-grader.bats` RG-1..15 pass against the head tree (RG-16/17 need the fixture corpus the snapshot lacks). No secrets, no new dependencies, no new network or exec sinks. Input handling added in this PR (`lib-content.sh` control-byte scrub, `rule_key` grammar, canonical-decimal index guard, `agent-types.yaml` key filter) is sound.

Two things block. First, the grader's new bare-`:N` citation rule treats the JSON pairs inside every review's LOA-VERDICT trailer (and markdown tokens such as `**Severity**:2`) as citations of the last cited file at lines 0–2, so a defect anchored near the top of that file is credited without being cited; reproduced head vs base. This grader produced the recall numbers behind the Task 4.8 revert in this same PR. Second, the gate rewrite keeps an undocumented `implement_gate.mode: authoritative` opt-in under which a model-authored `tool_input.active_skill` silently allows App Zone writes, while an Edit of `.loa.config.yaml` is itself a non-App-Zone write this hook allows silently in the head tree; reproduced end to end. The PR's own header states the field is model-authored and evidence-only.

**Phase 0 note.** `engineer-feedback.md` carries `CHANGES_REQUIRED`, not "All good"; the run-mode orchestrator requested this audit explicitly, so it ran as an independent gate and this deviation is recorded here. The known-failures surface was unreadable at session start (KF-SURFACE warning); triage proceeded without it. `br` is not installed, so the beads steps were skipped.

**Phase 1C dissent.** `adversarial-review.sh --type audit --diff-file pr/head.diff`: two voices (primary `gpt-5.5-pro` answered clean via `codex-headless`; companion `claude-headless` three findings), `consensus`, `voices_succeeded 2/2`, `rejected_summary` empty, `degraded: false`. Not a degraded security review. DISS-C-001 is confirmed below as MEDIUM-001; DISS-C-002 and DISS-C-003 are confirmed as LOW-002 and LOW-003.

**Security Issues Found:**
| Severity | Count |
|----------|-------|
| Critical | 0 |
| High | 1 |
| Medium | 2 |
| Low | 5 |

---

## Critical Security Issues (Must Fix)

None.

---

## High Priority Security Issues (Fix Before Deployment)

### [HIGH-001] Eval grader credits phantom citations from the LOA-VERDICT trailer and markdown tokens

**Severity:** HIGH (confidence: high)
**File:** `head/evals/graders/recall-vs-defects.sh:74`
**Issue:** The 1.1.0 parser adds a bare-`:N` alternative:

```
r'|(?:(?<![A-Za-z0-9_./:])(?:head|base)|(?<![A-Za-z0-9_./:])):(?P<bare>' + RNG + r')(?![A-Za-z0-9])')
```

The negative lookbehind excludes word characters, `.`, `/` and `:` but not `"`, `*`, `)`, `]`, `{` or `,`. Every `"critical":0`, `"high":1`, `"medium":0`, `"low":2`, `"excluded":0` pair in the trailer that every Loa review ends with, and tokens like `**Severity**:2`, `(see):1`, `"count":3`, therefore match and bind to the most recent cited path (`:84`) as citations at lines 0–2.

Reproduced against `pr/head/` and `pr/base/` with a two-defect manifest (anchors 3 and 400) and a review citing only `head/.claude/scripts/a.sh:400` followed by the standard trailer:

```
head 1.1.0: {"pass": true,  "score": 100, "detected": ["D-early","D-late"], "citations": 6}
base 1.0.0: {"pass": false, "score": 50,  "detected": ["D-late"], "missed": ["D-early"], "citations": 1}
```

Without a trailer, `**Severity**:2 and "count":3 and (see):1` after the same citation gives `citations: 4` and detects D-early; on a clean fixture without a trailer the false-positive count doubles (2 vs 1 on base).

**Impact:** Any defect whose anchor (or any `anchors[]` site) lies within lines 0–5 of the last file a review cites is credited unconditionally; `details.citations` is inflated on every trailer-bearing review; the no-trailer false-positive path over-counts. This grader is the measurement behind the pre-registered replay A/B rule that Task 4.8 used, in this PR, to revert the Sprint 3 trim and twelve rationales, and it is the fixture corpus's recall metric going forward. RG-1..15 pass on head only because no fixture anchor lies within lines 0–5 of the last cited file; no test places the mandated trailer after a citation with an early anchor.

**Fix:**

```python
# strip the trailer before citation parsing (it is parsed separately at `tm = re.search`)
text_for_cites = re.sub(r'<!-- LOA-VERDICT \{.*?\} -->', '', text, flags=re.S)
# and/or widen the lookbehind
r'(?<![A-Za-z0-9_./:"\'*(){}\[\],])'
```

Add an RG test: review `a.sh:400` plus the standard trailer must yield `citations == 1` and must not detect an anchor at line ≤ 5 of `a.sh`; add a no-trailer case with `**Bold**:2`. Re-run the replay A/B with the corrected grader and record whether the Task 4.8 revert stands.

**Reference:** CWE-1286 Improper Validation of Syntactic Correctness of Input — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/1286.html

---

## Medium Priority Issues

### [MEDIUM-001] Undocumented `implement_gate.mode: authoritative` turns a model-authored field into authorization, and the opt-in file is unfenced by this hook

**Severity:** MEDIUM (confidence: high) — Confirmed by cross-model review (DISS-C-001, `claude-headless`)
**File:** `head/.claude/hooks/compliance/implement-gate.sh:115` (selector), `:128-129` (silent allow), `head/tests/unit/implement-gate.bats:151-153` (IG-11 pins the key undocumented)
**Issue:**

```bash
configured_mode=$(yq '.implement_gate.mode // ""' "$PROJECT_ROOT/.loa.config.yaml" 2>/dev/null) || configured_mode=""
[[ "${configured_mode//\"/}" == "authoritative" ]] && compliance_mode="authoritative"
…
            implement|/implement|bug|/bug|run|/run|simstim|/simstim)
                exit 0
```

The PR's header (`:9-13`) states the PreToolUse payload carries no harness-set skill field and `tool_input` is model-authored. In authoritative mode that field alone allows an App Zone write with no RUNNING state. `.loa.config.yaml` sits at the project root, outside the App Zone; in the head tree a Write/Edit to it reaches "Non-App-Zone writes always allowed" (`:108`) and exits silently. The live install this audit runs on has a later revision that lists `.loa.config.yaml` as a trust input (ask); the PR as frozen does not.

Reproduced on `pr/head/` in a scratch project with no `.run/` state:

```
step 1  Edit {file_path: <root>/.loa.config.yaml, …}                     → exit 0, no output (silent allow)
        (file now holds: implement_gate:\n  mode: authoritative)
step 2  Write {file_path: <root>/src/index.ts, active_skill: "implement"} → exit 0, no output (silent allow)
control same Write without the key                                         → {"decision":"ask","reason":"[ADVISORY] …"}
```

**Impact:** The fenced agent (or a prompt-injected session) can switch the fence off and then self-attest on every App Zone write; no `ask` is raised and nothing is logged on the allow path. The base tree was bypassable through `.run/` files in the same way, so this PR narrows the selector rather than widening it, but it chooses to keep the self-attestation branch, keep the key out of every operator-facing document, and pin that choice with a test. A fence that is weakened by a hidden key is a Think-Before-Coding gap as much as an authz one.

**Fix:** Remove the authoritative branch until a harness-set field exists (the PR's own rationale). If it must stay: require RUNNING state AND the attestation; treat `.loa.config.yaml` (and `.run/platform-features.json`) as trust inputs that `ask` in this hook; write a `compliance.mode.model_signal` row to `audit.jsonl` on every authoritative allow; document the key with its warning in `.loa.config.yaml.example` and drop IG-11.

**Reference:** CWE-807 Reliance on Untrusted Inputs in a Security Decision — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/807.html; OWASP A01:2021 Broken Access Control — https://owasp.org/Top10/A01_2021-Broken_Access_Control/

### [MEDIUM-002] Catalog encodes two incompatible long-context pricing models for one vendor family

**Severity:** MEDIUM (confidence: high) — Confirmed by cross-model review (review-phase DISS-C-002)
**File:** `head/.claude/defaults/model-config.yaml:470-509` (new entry), `:562` (first fallback hop keeps the tier), `head/.claude/adapters/tests/test_anthropic_catalog_floor.py:326` and `:348`
**Issue:** The `claude-opus-5-5` entry omits `pricing.long_context`, citing the vendor page: `"Claude 4.6 and later models … include the full 1M token context window at standard pricing", so no long_context tier` (`:473-475`). Its first fallback hop `claude-opus-5` (`:562`), and `claude-sonnet-5`, `claude-fable-5`, `claude-fable-5-1`, keep `long_context: {threshold_tokens: 200000, input_multiplier: 2.0, output_multiplier: 1.5, verified: false}` from the same vendor source. `test_five_family_declares_the_beta_header_list_and_the_long_context_tier` (`:326`) pins the tier on FIVE_FAMILY; the new `test_opus_5_5_has_the_1m_window_at_standard_pricing` (`:348`) pins its absence on 5.5. FIVE_FAMILY excludes 5.5, so both tests pass and the contradiction is locked in.
**Impact:** A request that falls from `opus` to its first hop above 200K input is metered at twice the primary's cost (or the primary is under-metered); budget guards and cost tables tuned on one hop misfire on the other; the migration addendum (`head/docs/migration/v2.0-model-generation-floor.md:245-247`) documents one side only.
**Fix:** Decide once for the 4.6+ family: drop `long_context` from the FIVE_FAMILY entries and update `:326`, or add it to 5.5 with `verified: false` and record in catalog-evidence.md why the vendor statement is not trusted.
**Reference:** CWE-1068 Inconsistency Between Implementation and Documented Design — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/1068.html

---

## Low Priority Issues

### [LOW-001] `rule_key "$perm"` is a bare call under `set -euo pipefail`
- **Severity:** LOW (confidence: high)
- **File:** `head/.claude/scripts/check-permissions.sh:235`
- **Issue:** `rule_key` returns 1 for anything not shaped `Bash(…)` (`:164`). ### [HIGH-001] Eval grader credits phantom citations from the LOA-VERDICT trailer and markdown tokens

**Severity:** HIGH (confidence: high)
**File:** `head/evals/graders/recall-vs-defects.sh:74`
**Issue:** The 1.1.0 parser adds a bare-`:N` alternative:

```
r'|(?:(?<![A-Za-z0-9_./:])(?:head|base)|(?<![A-Za-z0-9_./:])):(?P<bare>' + RNG + r')(?![A-Za-z0-9])')
```

The negative lookbehind excludes word characters, `.`, `/` and `:` but not `"`, `*`, `)`, `]`, `{` or `,`. Every `"critical":0`, `"high":1`, `"medium":0`, `"low":2`, `"excluded":0` pair in the trailer that every Loa review ends with, and tokens like `**Severity**:2`, `(see):1`, `"count":3`, therefore match and bind to the most recent cited path (`:84`) as citations at lines 0–2.

Reproduced against `pr/head/` and `pr/base/` with a two-defect manifest (anchors 3 and 400) and a review citing only `head/.claude/scripts/a.sh:400` followed by the standard trailer:

```
head 1.1.0: {"pass": true,  "score": 100, "detected": ["D-early","D-late"], "citations": 6}
base 1.0.0: {"pass": false, "score": 50,  "detected": ["D-late"], "missed": ["D-early"], "citations": 1}
```

Without a trailer, `**Severity**:2 and "count":3 and (see):1` after the same citation gives `citations: 4` and detects D-early; on a clean fixture without a trailer the false-positive count doubles (2 vs 1 on base).

**Impact:** Any defect whose anchor (or any `anchors[]` site) lies within lines 0–5 of the last file a review cites is credited unconditionally; `details.citations` is inflated on every trailer-bearing review; the no-trailer false-positive path over-counts. This grader is the measurement behind the pre-registered replay A/B rule that Task 4.8 used, in this PR, to revert the Sprint 3 trim and twelve rationales, and it is the fixture corpus's recall metric going forward. RG-1..15 pass on head only because no fixture anchor lies within lines 0–5 of the last cited file; no test places the mandated trailer after a citation with an early anchor.

**Fix:**

```python
# strip the trailer before citation parsing (it is parsed separately at `tm = re.search`)
text_for_cites = re.sub(r'<!-- LOA-VERDICT \{.*?\} -->', '', text, flags=re.S)
# and/or widen the lookbehind
r'(?<![A-Za-z0-9_./:"\'*(){}\[\],])'
```

Add an RG test: review `a.sh:400` plus the standard trailer must yield `citations == 1` and must not detect an anchor at line ≤ 5 of `a.sh`; add a no-trailer case with `**Bold**:2`. Re-run the replay A/B with the corrected grader and record whether the Task 4.8 revert stands.

**Reference:** CWE-1286 Improper Validation of Syntactic Correctness of Input — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/1286.html

### [MEDIUM-001] Undocumented `implement_gate.mode: authoritative` turns a model-authored field into authorization, and the opt-in file is unfenced by this hook

**Severity:** MEDIUM (confidence: high) — Confirmed by cross-model review (DISS-C-001, `claude-headless`)
**File:** `head/.claude/hooks/compliance/implement-gate.sh:115` (selector), `:128-129` (silent allow), `head/tests/unit/implement-gate.bats:151-153` (IG-11 pins the key undocumented)
**Issue:**

```bash
configured_mode=$(yq '.implement_gate.mode // ""' "$PROJECT_ROOT/.loa.config.yaml" 2>/dev/null) || configured_mode=""
[[ "${configured_mode//\"/}" == "authoritative" ]] && compliance_mode="authoritative"
…
            implement|/implement|bug|/bug|run|/run|simstim|/simstim)
                exit 0
```

The PR's header (`:9-13`) states the PreToolUse payload carries no harness-set skill field and `tool_input` is model-authored. In authoritative mode that field alone allows an App Zone write with no RUNNING state. `.loa.config.yaml` sits at the project root, outside the App Zone; in the head tree a Write/Edit to it reaches "Non-App-Zone writes always allowed" (`:108`) and exits silently. The live install this audit runs on has a later revision that lists `.loa.config.yaml` as a trust input (ask); the PR as frozen does not.

Reproduced on `pr/head/` in a scratch project with no `.run/` state:

```
step 1  Edit {file_path: <root>/.loa.config.yaml, …}                     → exit 0, no output (silent allow)
        (file now holds: implement_gate:\n  mode: authoritative)
step 2  Write {file_path: <root>/src/index.ts, active_skill: "implement"} → exit 0, no output (silent allow)
control same Write without the key                                         → {"decision":"ask","reason":"[ADVISORY] …"}
```

**Impact:** The fenced agent (or a prompt-injected session) can switch the fence off and then self-attest on every App Zone write; no `ask` is raised and nothing is logged on the allow path. The base tree was bypassable through `.run/` files in the same way, so this PR narrows the selector rather than widening it, but it chooses to keep the self-attestation branch, keep the key out of every operator-facing document, and pin that choice with a test. A fence that is weakened by a hidden key is a Think-Before-Coding gap as much as an authz one.

**Fix:** Remove the authoritative branch until a harness-set field exists (the PR's own rationale). If it must stay: require RUNNING state AND the attestation; treat `.loa.config.yaml` (and `.run/platform-features.json`) as trust inputs that `ask` in this hook; write a `compliance.mode.model_signal` row to `audit.jsonl` on every authoritative allow; document the key with its warning in `.loa.config.yaml.example` and drop IG-11.

**Reference:** CWE-807 Reliance on Untrusted Inputs in a Security Decision — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/807.html; OWASP A01:2021 Broken Access Control — https://owasp.org/Top10/A01_2021-Broken_Access_Control/

## High Priority Security Issues (Fix Before Deployment)

### [HIGH-001] Eval grader credits phantom citations from the LOA-VERDICT trailer and markdown tokens

**Severity:** HIGH (confidence: high)
**File:** `head/evals/graders/recall-vs-defects.sh:74`
**Issue:** The 1.1.0 parser adds a bare-`:N` alternative:

```
r'|(?:(?<![A-Za-z0-9_./:])(?:head|base)|(?<![A-Za-z0-9_./:])):(?P<bare>' + RNG + r')(?![A-Za-z0-9])')
```

The negative lookbehind excludes word characters, `.`, `/` and `:` but not `"`, `*`, `)`, `]`, `{` or `,`. Every `"critical":0`, `"high":1`, `"medium":0`, `"low":2`, `"excluded":0` pair in the trailer that every Loa review ends with, and tokens like `**Severity**:2`, `(see):1`, `"count":3`, therefore match and bind to the most recent cited path (`:84`) as citations at lines 0–2.

Reproduced against `pr/head/` and `pr/base/` with a two-defect manifest (anchors 3 and 400) and a review citing only `head/.claude/scripts/a.sh:400` followed by the standard trailer:

```
head 1.1.0: {"pass": true,  "score": 100, "detected": ["D-early","D-late"], "citations": 6}
base 1.0.0: {"pass": false, "score": 50,  "detected": ["D-late"], "missed": ["D-early"], "citations": 1}
```

Without a trailer, `**Severity**:2 and "count":3 and (see):1` after the same citation gives `citations: 4` and detects D-early; on a clean fixture without a trailer the false-positive count doubles (2 vs 1 on base).

**Impact:** Any defect whose anchor (or any `anchors[]` site) lies within lines 0–5 of the last file a review cites is credited unconditionally; `details.citations` is inflated on every trailer-bearing review; the no-trailer false-positive path over-counts. This grader is the measurement behind the pre-registered replay A/B rule that Task 4.8 used, in this PR, to revert the Sprint 3 trim and twelve rationales, and it is the fixture corpus's recall metric going forward. RG-1..15 pass on head only because no fixture anchor lies within lines 0–5 of the last cited file; no test places the mandated trailer after a citation with an early anchor.

**Fix:**

```python
# strip the trailer before citation parsing (it is parsed separately at `tm = re.search`)
text_for_cites = re.sub(r'<!-- LOA-VERDICT \{.*?\} -->', '', text, flags=re.S)
# and/or widen the lookbehind
r'(?<![A-Za-z0-9_./:"\'*(){}\[\],])'
```

Add an RG test: review `a.sh:400` plus the standard trailer must yield `citations == 1` and must not detect an anchor at line ≤ 5 of `a.sh`; add a no-trailer case with `**Bold**:2`. Re-run the replay A/B with the corrected grader and record whether the Task 4.8 revert stands.

**Reference:** CWE-1286 Improper Validation of Syntactic Correctness of Input — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/1286.html

## Medium Priority Issues

### [MEDIUM-001] Undocumented `implement_gate.mode: authoritative` turns a model-authored field into authorization, and the opt-in file is unfenced by this hook

**Severity:** MEDIUM (confidence: high) — Confirmed by cross-model review (DISS-C-001, `claude-headless`)
**File:** `head/.claude/hooks/compliance/implement-gate.sh:115` (selector), `:128-129` (silent allow), `head/tests/unit/implement-gate.bats:151-153` (IG-11 pins the key undocumented)
**Issue:**

```bash
configured_mode=$(yq '.implement_gate.mode // ""' "$PROJECT_ROOT/.loa.config.yaml" 2>/dev/null) || configured_mode=""
[[ "${configured_mode//\"/}" == "authoritative" ]] && compliance_mode="authoritative"
…
            implement|/implement|bug|/bug|run|/run|simstim|/simstim)
                exit 0
```

The PR's header (`:9-13`) states the PreToolUse payload carries no harness-set skill field and `tool_input` is model-authored. In authoritative mode that field alone allows an App Zone write with no RUNNING state. `.loa.config.yaml` sits at the project root, outside the App Zone; in the head tree a Write/Edit to it reaches "Non-App-Zone writes always allowed" (`:108`) and exits silently. The live install this audit runs on has a later revision that lists `.loa.config.yaml` as a trust input (ask); the PR as frozen does not.

Reproduced on `pr/head/` in a scratch project with no `.run/` state:

```
step 1  Edit {file_path: <root>/.loa.config.yaml, …}                     → exit 0, no output (silent allow)
        (file now holds: implement_gate:\n  mode: authoritative)
step 2  Write {file_path: <root>/src/index.ts, active_skill: "implement"} → exit 0, no output (silent allow)
control same Write without the key                                         → {"decision":"ask","reason":"[ADVISORY] …"}
```

**Impact:** The fenced agent (or a prompt-injected session) can switch the fence off and then self-attest on every App Zone write; no `ask` is raised and nothing is logged on the allow path. The base tree was bypassable through `.run/` files in the same way, so this PR narrows the selector rather than widening it, but it chooses to keep the self-attestation branch, keep the key out of every operator-facing document, and pin that choice with a test. A fence that is weakened by a hidden key is a Think-Before-Coding gap as much as an authz one.

**Fix:** Remove the authoritative branch until a harness-set field exists (the PR's own rationale). If it must stay: require RUNNING state AND the attestation; treat `.loa.config.yaml` (and `.run/platform-features.json`) as trust inputs that `ask` in this hook; write a `compliance.mode.model_signal` row to `audit.jsonl` on every authoritative allow; document the key with its warning in `.loa.config.yaml.example` and drop IG-11.

**Reference:** CWE-807 Reliance on Untrusted Inputs in a Security Decision — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/807.html; OWASP A01:2021 Broken Access Control — https://owasp.org/Top10/A01_2021-Broken_Access_Control/

### [MEDIUM-002] Catalog encodes two incompatible long-context pricing models for one vendor family

**Severity:** MEDIUM (confidence: high) — Confirmed by cross-model review (review-phase DISS-C-002)
**File:** `head/.claude/defaults/model-config.yaml:470-509` (new entry), `:562` (first fallback hop keeps the tier), `head/.claude/adapters/tests/test_anthropic_catalog_floor.py:326` and `:348`
**Issue:** The `claude-opus-5-5` entry omits `pricing.long_context`, citing the vendor page: `"Claude 4.6 and later models … include the full 1M token context window at standard pricing", so no long_context tier` (`:473-475`). Its first fallback hop `claude-opus-5` (`:562`), and `claude-sonnet-5`, `claude-fable-5`, `claude-fable-5-1`, keep `long_context: {threshold_tokens: 200000, input_multiplier: 2.0, output_multiplier: 1.5, verified: false}` from the same vendor source. `test_five_family_declares_the_beta_header_list_and_the_long_context_tier` (`:326`) pins the tier on FIVE_FAMILY; the new `test_opus_5_5_has_the_1m_window_at_standard_pricing` (`:348`) pins its absence on 5.5. FIVE_FAMILY excludes 5.5, so both tests pass and the contradiction is locked in.
**Impact:** A request that falls from `opus` to its first hop above 200K input is metered at twice the primary's cost (or the primary is under-metered); budget guards and cost tables tuned on one hop misfire on the other; the migration addendum (`head/docs/migration/v2.0-model-generation-floor.md:245-247`) documents one side only.
**Fix:** Decide once for the 4.6+ family: drop `long_context` from the FIVE_FAMILY entries and update `:326`, or add it to 5.5 with `verified: false` and record in catalog-evidence.md why the vendor statement is not trusted.

# Retrospective Postlude Template

**Version**: 1.0.0
**Purpose**: Embed at END of SKILL.md files for invisible learning extraction

---

## Usage

Copy the `<retrospective_postlude>` section below and paste it at the very END of any skill's SKILL.md file, after all main skill content.

---

## Template

```xml
<retrospective_postlude>
## Invisible Retrospective

After completing main skill logic, scan session for learning opportunities.

**CRITICAL**: This postlude executes SILENTLY. Only surface findings that pass quality gates.

### Step 1: Check Configuration

Read `.loa.config.yaml`:
```yaml
invisible_retrospective:
  enabled: true|false
  skills:
    {current-skill-name}: true|false
```

The effective `enabled` value is the explicit key, else the `loa.profile` default: `.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh knob invisible_retrospective.enabled true`.

**Exit Conditions** (skip all processing if any are true):
- the effective `invisible_retrospective.enabled` is not `true` → Log action: DISABLED, exit
- `invisible_retrospective.skills.{this-skill}: false` → Log action: DISABLED, exit
- **RECURSION GUARD**: This skill is `continuous-learning` → Exit silently (prevent infinite recursion)
  - INVARIANT: The `continuous-learning` skill MUST NEVER have a retrospective postlude
  - The schema also excludes `continuous-learning` from valid skill values

### Step 2: Scan Session for Learning Signals

Search the current conversation for these patterns:

| Signal | Detection Patterns | Weight |
|--------|-------------------|--------|
| Error Resolution | "error", "failed", "fixed", "resolved", "worked", "the issue was" | 3 |
| Multiple Attempts | "tried", "attempted", "finally", "after several", "on the Nth try" | 3 |
| Unexpected Behavior | "surprisingly", "actually", "turns out", "discovered", "realized" | 2 |
| Workaround Found | "instead", "alternative", "workaround", "bypass", "the trick is" | 2 |
| Pattern Discovery | "pattern", "convention", "always", "never", "this codebase" | 1 |

**Scoring**: Sum weights for each candidate discovery.

**Output**: List of candidate discoveries (max 5 per skill invocation, from config `max_candidates`)

If no candidates found:
- Log action: SKIPPED, candidates_found: 0

The audit is complete and the feedback file is written and self-checked.

**Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED** for sprint-1 (PR cycle-126 sprint-250 tasks 4.1–4.8). Feedback is at `grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/auditor-sprint-feedback.md`, ending with the LOA-VERDICT trailer. The trailer self-check passed (consistent, exit 0, excluded_confirmed matches the review's excluded of 0).

| Severity | Count |
|----------|-------|
| Critical | 0 |
| High | 1 |
| Medium | 2 |
| Low | 5 |

**Blocking findings**

- **HIGH, grader phantom citations** at `head/evals/graders/recall-vs-defects.sh:74`. The new bare-`:N` rule binds the JSON pairs in every review's verdict trailer, and markdown tokens like bold labels, to the last cited file at lines 0–2. Reproduced on head vs base: recall 1.0 with 6 citations versus 0.5 with 1 citation for the same review. The Task 4.8 revert in this PR rests on numbers from this grader.
- **MEDIUM, gate opt-in is self-attestable** at `head/.claude/hooks/compliance/implement-gate.sh:115`. An undocumented config key makes a model-authored field an authorization signal, and in the head tree an Edit of that config file is a non-App-Zone write the same hook allows silently. Reproduced end to end: config edit allowed, then an App Zone write with a self-attested skill allowed, while the control case asks. Confirmed by the companion dissent voice.
- **MEDIUM, long-context pricing contradiction** at `head/.claude/defaults/model-config.yaml:470`. Opus 5.5 has no long-context tier citing a vendor statement about 4.6+ models, while its first fallback hop and the rest of the 5 family keep a 2x/1.5x tier from the same source. Tests pin both states.

**Low findings** cover two dead-path bugs in the permission checker, the headless model's permissions row claiming no side effects, 15 bytes of prompt-budget headroom, and a registry gap for a project agent present on this install.

**Process notes**

- The review gate had not approved the sprint, so the skill's Phase 0 prerequisite was not met. The orchestrator requested the audit explicitly, so it ran as an independent gate and the deviation is recorded in the report.
- The dissent ran with two voices in consensus, no rejected payloads, not degraded. The primary was clean. All three companion findings were confirmed and tallied.
- Verified clean: managed-file hash and catalog checksum recompute, the PR's gate tests pass on the head tree, no secrets or new sinks.
- Beads is not installed, so the beads steps were skipped. The known-failures surface was unreadable at session start.
- Supporting artifacts are in `grimoires/loa/a2a/audits/2026-10-21/` and the trajectory logs. A stray log directory my test run created under the PR snapshot was removed, so `pr/` is unchanged.

Next step for the sprint is a fix round through the implement, review and audit cycle, with the grader fix first and the replay A/B re-run with the corrected grader.
